text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.2% today, continuing a steep two-week decline of 8.2% that accelerated sharply on November 2nd. The primary driver was crude oil dropping more than 7% Monday on hopes of U.S.-Iran peace talks, which would ease geopolitical tensions that have supported elevated oil prices. Since refiners like Marathon profit from the difference between crude costs and refined product prices, a sudden oil price collapse compresses those margins and immediately pressures the stock, even as refineries continue running at a healthy 92.8% capacity.

The decline also reflects broader caution among investors ahead of Big Oil earnings, where guidance on future profitability matters as much as current results. The company announced a leadership change on October 29th, adding uncertainty at a time when oil price direction—now swinging on diplomatic news rather than supply fundamentals—has become the dominant driver of refiner valuations.
